name: Kim Il-sung
role: Founder and supreme leader of North Korea (1948-1994)
summary: Kim Il-sung led North Korea's one-party socialist state under the Juche idea of independence in politics, self-sustenance in the economy and self-defence. His own works defend state and cooperative ownership, central planning, party leadership and a strengthening state, while calling for a federal, neutral reunified Korea free of foreign troops. The reference record adds purges of rivals, a personality cult and hereditary succession.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 1967 government programme cites universal free medical care as an achievement of the system, and his 1980 programme promises medical treatment for all working people and their families.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Built a state-planned economy, called individual farming incapable of modernization and urged socialist countries to keep collective farms, and contrasted the capitalist market with the socialist one.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalized the industries, transport, communications and banks of the Japanese and collaborators in 1946, treating them as property of the people.

property-fundamental.rationale: Confiscated landlords' land without compensation and described socialist reorganization as freeing production from 'private ownership'; the 1993 programme recognises private property only as a condition of reunification.

cut-welfare.rationale: Presented free education, free medical care, state nurseries and the abolition of taxes as achievements; his programmes expand state guarantees of livelihood rather than cut them.

state-harmful.rationale: Insisted on strengthening the party and the people's power and treated a strong state as essential against imperialist encirclement.

empower-police-military.rationale: Programme of self-defence in national defence: arm the workers, fortify the country, keep increasing military power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Condemned licensed and unlicensed prostitution under the US occupation of the South as humiliation of women, without discussing legality for consenting adults.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Criticized officials who ignored national history and culture and ordered systematic study of Korea's cultural heritage.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Said his 'radiochemical laboratory' is an element of a peaceful nuclear power industry and welcomed light-water reactors.

revolution-justified.rationale: Said he took the road of revolution at thirteen and urged revolutionaries to carry on to the last, and praised the armed revolution that overthrew Batista in Cuba.

central-planning.rationale: Ran a command economy of state plans (planning commissions, manpower planning, national plans) and cited full employment and no beggars as proof it worked, including to the end in 1994.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributed land to tillers in 1946 but then collectivized it, seeking all-people and cooperative property.

one-party-rule.rationale: Merged the communist and new democratic parties into a single Workers' Party and said a working-class party must hold political leadership, faulting the Soviet party for giving it up.

democracy-best.rationale: Called democracy a common ideal and his system democratic, yet judged multi-party reform in Eastern Europe a ruin.

political-violence-never.rationale: Founded and led the anti-Japanese armed struggle, upheld armed revolution and the dictatorship over class enemies, and praised armed struggle against US imperialism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Held defence to be a state task of self-reliance and nationwide mobilization.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Boasted that no one is particularly rich or poor and everyone lives equally.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Called selfish desire to work for one's own interests a revisionist survival that clashes with communist ideas.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Called work a sacred duty and defined human rights in collective terms of people as social beings.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Aimed to eliminate the distinction between mental and physical labour and between town and country as part of communism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He stated distribution according to work as the socialist principle; no statement of the ultimate rule found.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Described capitalist exploitation as a naked, direct form of exploitation, said socialism ends the exploitation of man by man, and identified owners and landlords as exploiter classes.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Called the organs of people's government organs of the dictatorship of the proletariat, and said socialist democracy presupposes dictatorship of the working people over their class enemies.

collective-farming.rationale: Led the collectivization of agriculture, told a visiting Czechoslovak leader not to dissolve cooperative farms but turn them into all-people farms, and argued individual farming blocks irrigation and mechanization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Said it is in the nature of imperialism to commit aggression and plunder and that it will not change before it dies; he did not frame it as wars among great powers.

taxation-theft.rationale: Treated the state's agricultural tax in kind as a legitimate use for national development, unlike colonial tax.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Said rights are those of people as social beings and that American-style individual human rights do not suit his country.

positive-liberty.rationale: Defined human rights as rights to work, rest, education and medical care and said political freedom requires equal material and cultural life.

total-state.rationale: The state and party directed the economy, state schooling and propaganda and culture.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Described the Arab struggle against 'Israeli aggressors' as part of the anti-imperialist front, without discussing a Jewish state in principle.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Proposed guaranteeing all overseas compatriots the right to return to the homeland and live where they choose.

school-vouchers.rationale: Built a state education system funded and run by the state and rejected diverting it.

national-self-determination.rationale: Held that every nation has the right to independence and to decide its own destiny, and called division by outsiders illegitimate.

class-collaboration.rationale: Welcomed patriotic capitalists into a united front and a federal state, yet taught that acute class struggle continues under socialism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Ordered the cultural heritage to be publicised and studied rather than discarded.

dominated-front.rationale: Urged non-aligned and developing countries to unite against imperialism and domination, destroy the old economic order and cooperate.

workers-nation.rationale: Said patriotism and internationalism must go together, and that revolution should be carried out by each nation's own people.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Promoted equal rights for women with men in all spheres and state nurseries so women could work.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the organs of his own state as instruments of the dictatorship of the proletariat and called imperialist and comprador governments tools of exploiters.

national-mission.rationale: Said revolution can be neither exported nor imported and that each country must find its own way.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said the old order humiliated and oppressed women twofold and threefold, and that the new state freed them.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said Soviet-bloc parties exercised bureaucracy, lost touch with the people and perished; also warned about bureaucracy in his own officials.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ran a state that directs the economy, education and welfare, with the government providing housing, health and schooling.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Said in 1968 that final victory requires ending encirclement across countries, but in 1990-94 said Korean socialism stands independently and is unshakable.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Said countries holding power amid capitalist encirclement face aggression and restoration of capitalism throughout the transition, and vowed to keep strengthening the party and the people's power.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Led armed struggle and authorized the 1950 invasion, while declaring peaceful reunification his consistent policy.

vanguard-party.rationale: Called the Workers' Party an organized combat unit and vanguard of the working masses that must keep iron discipline and monolithic ideology.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His programmes put the poor's livelihood first, raising their living standards to the middle class and backing poor peasants and fishermen.

party-controls-media.rationale: Treated newspapers as organs of party propaganda: criticized the party's propaganda department for forbidding papers to carry articles and directed what they should publicise.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Demanded unity of ideology and will and iron discipline in party ranks, and a fight against every tendency incompatible with them.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Held top office continuously from 1948 until death in 1994, including president from 1972, under a system with no term limits.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Proposed a neutral, non-aligned unified Korea that repeals the military treaties of both halves, though the DPRK itself kept treaties with China and the USSR.

people-in-arms.rationale: Called for workers and farmers to hold a sickle and a rifle and for the whole country to be a fortress, while keeping a large professional army.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Made reunification of Korea, divided by foreign forces in 1945, the central national task for five decades.

death-penalty.rationale: Pak Hon-yong, accused of spying for the US, was executed in 1955 after the campaign Kim led against spies; he gave no general statement on capital punishment.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Demanded monolithic ideology and will across the party and society, and campaigned against deviating tendencies.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Said the debt problem of developing countries should be solved fairly and completely, while proposing interest-free extension of repayment.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said fully independent state cannot be built without democratic reforms of land and industry, and that economic independence underlies political independence.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Told developed countries to assist third-world countries rather than expand armaments, while stressing developing countries' own efforts.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Said in 1994 that the DPRK has no nuclear weapons, will not have any, and pursues denuclearization of the peninsula, while rejecting inspections it saw as unfair.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Called both the Soviet Union and China socialist countries and fraternal states, and blamed leaders such as Gorbachev, not the system, for the Soviet collapse.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Proposed a Democratic Federal Republic of Koryo with two systems and two regional governments keeping their own ideologies and economies.

leader-cult.rationale: Reports in the reference source show statues and portraits from about 1949 and compulsory praise by the 1960s; he described the leader, party and masses as united in single-hearted unity and wrote eulogies of his son.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Held that exploiter classes try to recover lost positions and that capitalism can be restored, kept class struggle acute under socialist democracy, and blamed revisionism and weak party leadership for the Soviet and East European collapses.

land-redistribution.rationale: Confiscated landlords' and Japanese land without compensation and distributed it free to the peasants in the 1946 agrarian reform.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Called for unity of all Koreans in north, south and overseas into a single state on the principle of one nation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Held that the masses are makers of history and that man decides everything, and put ideological revolution ahead of material factors.

moral-incentives.rationale: Told cooperative farm officials that political and moral incentives come first and that relying on material incentives is a revisionist idea, though some material incentive is needed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Founded his own guerrilla army in 1932 and praised Che Guevara for organizing the masses to armed struggle, though he also stressed building mass support.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Demanded that propaganda and education centre on Korean history and the Korean revolution rather than foreign models.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Condemned colonial rule, including Japan's, as slavery and assimilation of Korea.

patriotic-education.rationale: Complained that schools hung portraits of foreigners and not Koreans, asking how children could develop national pride.

delink-world-market.rationale: Built an independent national economy but said it does not rule out economic cooperation, trade or joint ventures with other countries.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Said developing countries' resources and the fruits of their labour are snatched away cheaply by developed capitalist countries, widening the gap.

party-own-road.rationale: Held that each party must draw up policy independently for its own country and praised other parties for independence.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Built a doctrine of self-reliance and boasted of receiving no aid or foreign capital, but from 1992 welcomed joint ventures and foreign investment in free trade zones.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rejected Western human rights standards and said each country should build socialism its own way, not copy others.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Introduced state social insurance and promised welfare systems for workers rather than private accounts.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Said victorious revolutions should render active support to the liberation struggle of peoples with political, economic and military power.

job-guarantee.rationale: Promised work for all able-bodied people, and said there is no unemployment in the DPRK.

non-intervention.rationale: Endorsed non-interference in internal affairs as a principle of relations, while urging foreign campaigns to force the South Korean president out and calling for material support to liberation struggles.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Rejected 'worship of great powers' and sycophancy, and said even small states must not live subordinate to others.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: His 1980 programme protects personal effects alongside state and cooperative property; in the North he built socialist ownership of means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Said north and south should not seek to prevail over communism or communize each other, and kept socialism as a goal.

religion-illusion.rationale: He said 'we believe in Man, not in God' but did not call religion an illusion that will fade.

socialized-care.rationale: Praised nurseries and kindergartens run at state and community expense so women can join social labour, though not housework.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Called his system socialism and communism the goal and rejected a third way.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Purged rival factions, demanded an 'implacable fight' against tendencies against party unity, and introduced a monolithic ideological system; his 1980 and 1993 pledges of freedoms apply to a reunified federation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Denounced Japanese colonial plunder and US attempts to turn the South into a market and resource base.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Proposed that a united Korea be a neutral, non-aligned state like Austria and not a satellite of any power, and backed the non-aligned movement.

dynastic-succession.rationale: In 1994 he said his son Kim Jong Il had taken over his ideas and leadership and led party, state and army, and the party congress of 1980 had designated him successor.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Held that the socialist state, not charity, must guarantee livelihood, schooling and health.

term-limits.rationale: Held office for life under a system without term limits; he gave no statement on term limits themselves.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Proposed that a unified Korea ban foreign and nuclear weapons, and said he had worked to denuclearize the peninsula since US weapons arrived in the South.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: His 1980 programme bans foreign troops and bases in a unified Korea and demands US forces leave the South.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Described Koreans as a homogeneous nation descended from Tangun, living on the same land through the ages.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: His 1993 programme calls for honouring patriotic martyrs and their descendants.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Said only when a working-class party seizes power can it lead society, and defined his system as one where working people are masters of the state.

person-over-state.rationale: Said everything should serve man, yet subordinated individuals to collective goals and the party.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Pledged force only against attack in 1994, but authorized the 1950 invasion of South Korea per the reference source.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Argued Koreans are one homogeneous nation sharing land, language and culture, so division by outsiders and religions or systems does not split it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Said Korea was divided artificially by foreign forces and that the US manufactures 'two Koreas' and works to keep the South a colony.

free-public-college.rationale: Reported schooling, including 98 institutes of higher learning, free of charge, and defended free education at state expense.

arms-reduction.rationale: Proposed cutting both Korean armies to 100,000-150,000 each and abolishing nuclear weapons.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for a new, fair international economic order to replace the old, unequal one that exploits developing countries.

workers-own-party.rationale: Founded and led a separate Workers' Party of the working masses, independent of conservative parties.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1946 Law on Sex Equality gave women equal rights with men and a place in politics, and he cited it as emancipation.

close-ties-china.rationale: Called China a close neighbour and comrade-in-arms and cooperated closely with it; the DPRK signed a defence treaty with China in 1961.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Made the DFRK responsible for defending the national rights of all overseas Koreans.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Said taxes were abolished in the DPRK and presented that as an achievement.

national-resource-control.rationale: Condemned the sale of mining and trading concessions to American capital and called resources of developing countries to be kept from foreign capture.

multipolar-world.rationale: Said there cannot be major and minor countries, condemned superpower and dominationist politics, and called for an end to power politics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Argued that patriotism and the working class's international cause are parts of one revolutionary cause, and linked love of nation to service of working people.

notes: Works published under his name count as his words, whoever drafted them. Positions on reunification, nuclear weapons and foreign investment shifted by period; later statements are used. His 1980 and 1993 promises of freedoms and property protection apply to a reunified federation, not to the North, where the reference source records purges and a personality cult. No inferences were used.
